newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DALY GIVES A FEW BACK TO WINGED FOOT IN PGA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DALY GIVES A FEW BACK TO WINGED FOOT IN PGA.

text.p: John Daly gave a little back to Winged Foot on Friday but he still thinks he has a good chance to win his second PGA Chmpionship.

Daly, who opened the championship on Thursday with a record-tying four-under-par 66 and a share of the lead, slipped to a three-over 73 in the second round as Winged Foot's notorious greens got the better of him.
But the 31-year-old Daly, who burst onto the golf scene with a stunning victory in the 1991 PGA, was still one under par for the championship and he was neither disappointed nor discouraged.

"If anyone told me I would be one under after two days, I would have taken it," said Daly, a recovering alcoholic who walked off the course after 27 holes in the U.S. Open in June suffering from the effects of withdrawal.
Daly, who putted superbly in the opening round, said he found Winged Foot's slippery, sloping greens much more difficult to fathom on Friday.
"I hit a lot of good shots but I didn't make any putts," Daly said. "I missed a lot of four- and five-footers."
Daly, who had only two bogeys in his record-matching opening round, had six bogeys on Friday -- five on the back nine, which he said was playing much harder.
A comparision of how he played the last three holes -- each 448 yards or more -- each day probably tells the whole story.

The long-hitting Daly, who also won the 1995 British Open, birdied all three on Friday -- hitting two 9-irons and a wedge to the greens and leaving himself birdie putts of five and four feet on 16 and 17 -- and a tap-in at the difficult last.
Friday was a different story. With a breeze blowing against the players on the final three holes, Daly needed 6-iron, 7-iron and 5-iron to reach the greens -- and he could not get any very close.
"Those last three holes -- what a difference," Daly said. "They played like they're supposed to."
He bogeyed both the 16th and 18th, where he three-putted from about 60 feet.

"These greens have small breaks that you just don't see," Daly said after the second round. After the first round he said: "Every time I got on the green I just saw the line and putts started going in."
Daly said one reason his putts did not fall as frequently on Friday was that many holes were cut in more difficult positions, making approach shots more challenging and putts harder to read.
"The pins were very tough today," he said.
Still, Daly, who missed this year's Masters and British Open after undergoing alcohol rehabilitation, liked his position halfway through the last major championship of the year.
"Any time you're three or four shots out of the lead in a major, you have a chance," he said.
